obligations.obligation: must_include: The board and Pike's ledger anatomized on the page as mechanism — posting (holds, carters, brokers), taking, witnessing, completion entered in the ledger, price — shown through Pike's practice and Cael's cataloguing, not narrator exposition. No tier column; the board sorts by outcome.
obligations.evidence: Posting, by paper: 'The holds' slips were good stock, cut square, in a steady hand, with a mark burned into one corner — a brand ... The brokers' slips were the thin paper brokers used everywhere, in a clerk's hand, the price written twice, once in words. And the carters' slips were in Pike's hand — every one — ... because a carter came to the board and said what he wanted and Pike wrote it and read it back to him, and that was how a man who could not write posted a job.' Taking and witnessing, in Pike's own words: 'Crew that wants it marks the slip — first mark takes it, unless the hirer's named a crew, and the holds name crews. Then I write HOLD and whose. ... Whoever they did it for, or whoever took delivery, marks the slip and says what happened. No mark, no line.' Completion, staged twice in scene: the north-road captain's slip ('"Witness is the hold," Pike said ... "Escort. North road, two carts, grain. Delivered. No loss. Six marks." A pause. "Paid?" ... and the five columns took it — Job, Hirer, Witness, Outcome, Price') and the failed recovery ('"Eleven lost to the water. Nine recovered. Three marks of eight."' entered 'in the same ink, at the same size, as delivered, no loss'). Price: '"The hold says forty. The carter says nine." ... "if a crew asks me what a job's worth I'll tell it, and the two numbers aren't always the same number, and I don't make either of them come true."' Outcome-sort with no tier: the wall sheet ordered '"By me."' and 'ordered by him, on which a Bronze who lost a carter is under a Copper who brought one home'; the five columns named with no tier column; Cael's log restates the whole machine in his register.

Contiguous, in dialogue: '"A Bronze who lost my carter is worth less than a Copper who brought him home. Out here that's arithmetic. In there it was heresy." Pike said it without emphasis, at the pitch he said a price.' Prompted by Karis: '"A Bronze crew," Karis said, carefully, "and a Copper crew. Same road. You'd put—"'

obligations.obligation: must_include: The unit's standing stated honestly — unknown, cheap, taking the jobs the established crews don't want; Teague's crew eleven lines above them at the top of the column for three years.
obligations.evidence: Pike: '"Bottom." / "Why?" / "Four lines. Nobody lost, nobody hurt, nobody knows you." ... "Every job you've done was one nobody above you wanted. That's not a fault. That's what the bottom of the sheet's for." / "And the top?" / "Teague. Four with him. Three years."' Brom counts the distance at the plank ('"Eleven." ... "Lines," he said. "Between. If we're bottom and he's top."'); the wall confirms it ('Thirteen lines. ... at the bottom, in the same hand and the same ink and the same size as all the rest, five names in a row'); the log: 'Where we are on it: last. Thirteen lines and ours is the thirteenth. Eleven between us and a crew called Teague's — four people, three years at the top'. 'Cheap' is carried from Chapter 1 through the steading 'that had called them cheap and meant it' and 'a jug we can afford because of nine marks.'

obligations.obligation: must_include: The asset-restriction beat, once, over the board's map, with Seln's, Brom's, and Karis's lines as specified; then the map turned east; not revisited.
obligations.evidence: Over the carter's map on Pike's plank: 'He put one finger on the stroke and drew it down the sheet ... "West of that," he said, "the inventory executes the hour any of us shows paper. Pending jurisdiction means armed. Nobody goes west." / Brom, from the roof's edge, without turning: "Nobody wants to." / "Nobody can. Different sentences." Karis's pen had not moved.' Map turned: 'he took the stone off the map's corner and turned the sheet on the plank ... until the stroke lay along the edge nearest them and the roads ran away from it up the sheet, east'. Put away: 'Nobody said anything else about it.' The log refers to it once more only as a note that it was said and will not be said again ('I am noting once that it was said. The map's turned east.'); the beat itself is not restaged.

obligations.obligation: must_include: The first pole in the Power Log, mid-chapter (not at the end), honoring the card's entry.
obligations.evidence: At the inn table, in the fifth of six sections, with the full Teague section after it. The card's sentences verbatim inside a longer italic entry: '*No instrument out here reads me. No Arbiter station, no assessment panel, no registry seat with a seal on it. The board reads what we did. I've spent four years being the case the instruments couldn't parse, and it turns out the cure was a country with no instruments. Write it plainly, because it's true: I'm free. First time.*' Chosen and believed, in the permitted cataloguing form: 'He read it back once. The sentence was there, in his own hand, plain, and he let it stand, and noticed himself letting it, and did not argue with the noticing either.'

obligations.obligation: must_include: Teague's crew seen across the room at the best table (four practitioners; Teague: Force Path, Bronze-tier by a registry he stopped reporting to years ago; counts his people before he counts a job). Cael reads him; Teague reads them; no dialogue between them.
obligations.evidence: Four: 'Four. Road gear, worn to the shape of the people in it. Three first — a tall woman with a spear ...; a man Brom's height and half Brom's width, with a crossbow ...; a young man, twenty ... They went to the best table.' Counts his people first: 'He did not look at the room. He did not look at the wall, or at Pike, or at the ledger under its stone. He looked at the tall woman, and then at the man with the crossbow, and then at the young one — each, in turn, for the length of a breath ... and only when he had them, all three, at the table with the jug, did he step in off the sill'; and again with the slip: 'only when the young one had food in front of him did he look back down at the slip and read it.' Path and tier: 'Force Path. Cael had it from the doorway ... the weight down through the heels, the shoulders carried low and square, the hands loose — the same setting Pike sat in, except that this one had not stopped using it. Bronze, the book inside had said once, and would still say if anyone opened it, and nobody would. There was nothing on him a registry had given.' Pike's source for the tier and lapse: '"Force. Bronze — was, by the book inside. He stopped writing to it years ago and it stopped asking."' Mutual read: 'Cael watched him do it. He knew the method because it was his own ... He found Seln on the second pass' and 'he read the man back. Item. He had counted his people before he had counted the job ...'. No speech: 'Neither of them spoke. There was nothing to say that the wall had not said, and both of them knew where the wall was.'

obligations.obligation: must_include: The chapter ENDS on the image of Teague turning back to his table and the ledger on the wall with eleven lines between them — not on a log entry.
obligations.evidence: Final two paragraphs: 'Teague looked a moment longer. Then he took his two fingers off the slip, and turned, and went back to his table, and sat down among his three ...' and the last line of the file: 'The last of the day came through the gap in one flat bar and lay across the long wall, across the sheet pinned there at its four corners, and in that light he could read it from where he sat: the one word at the top, and their five names at the bottom, and between the two, in Pike's hand, eleven lines with the light on every one of them.' The log entry sits in the previous section; the closer is an observed image, which differs from Chapter 1's log closer (charter §9 scene-closer rule).

obligations.obligation: must_include: Cael's cataloguing habit on the page outside the log at least once (the board, the meadow, Pike's table, the room).
obligations.evidence: All four. The meadow: 'thirty-one tents and carts where there had been twenty-six, and of the twenty-six he could find nine.' The board: 'Sixteen slips where there had been fourteen. He read all sixteen, twice, and sorted. Seven escorts ... Three hold contracts, priced high, each with HOLD in Pike's hand'. Pike's table: 'a plank on two barrels. The ledger, open. An ink-pot, a pen, a knife for the pen. A river stone the size of a fist ... A cup. Nothing else. The pinned sleeve. The weight all the way down.' The room: 'Long, low, six tables. Fire at the far end, the best table beside it — four chairs, empty ... And on the wall between the fire and the door ... one sheet. He counted before he read, because counting was faster and he wanted the number first. Thirteen lines.' Plus the itemized read of Teague ('Item. He had counted his people before he had counted the job ...').

obligations.obligation: must_include: Each companion in their own register at least once — Lira kinetic and blunt; Brom weight, few words; Karis precise, note-taking; Seln procedural, dry, never explaining himself.
obligations.evidence: Lira: 'Lira's foot, which had been moving since they reached the landing, stopped.' / '"Where are we," Lira said. Brom: 'Brom looked at it for a while, chose another ten paces on, and put the boxes down, and that was the end of the matter.' / '"He's still standing there."' / '"Nobody wants to."' / '"Eleven." ... obligations.obligation: payoff: Vell's ledger doctrine (Book 1) recognized at country scale by a man who never heard of Vell.
obligations.evidence: Immediately after Pike's pricing line: 'Cael had been fourteen at a table in Ardenmere with a woman on the far side of it and a bound book between them, and he had learned there, over one season, that a ledger could be the only honest record of a person ... And here it was, whole, run as a system at the scale of a country by a one-armed man on two barrels ... He saw the shape of it entire and did not say so. He said the other thing. / "Did you ever hear of a ledger-keeper called Vell?" / "No." / "No reason you would."' This was a margin note in a board-keeper's ledger. He did not rank the two. He noticed that he did not.'

inventions: Return timing: the unit crosses the Thornwater stretch at midday on Seln's instruction (his reason unstated) and reaches Lowmarch on the forty-ninth day past the Line; the valley makes its ordinary noise the whole way and nothing paces them. The Chapter 1 hypothesis is repeated as 'Something out here hunted Paths. Ruling: hold.' and not advanced.

Lowmarch texture within the allowed set: the river lower and the ford's poles standing higher; the meadow turned over (thirty-one tents and carts, nine of the original twenty-six still present); the unit's spot under an ash taken by a carter, Brom choosing another; the lower inn's common room as 'the board's room' because Pike carries the ledger up from the landing at dusk; the wall sheet — one page in Pike's hand, pinned with wooden pegs, thirteen crews ordered by Pike's judgment, holds asking 'who' at the ferry and taking the top of the sheet.

The board's postings as objects: three kinds of paper — holds' good stock with a burned brand in the corner (a hold has a fire and an iron and no seal), brokers' thin clerk-hand slips with the price written twice, carters' slips written by Pike on the backs of older slips because carters cannot write. Sixteen slips now (seven escorts, two fence-lines, two recoveries, three hold contracts, the ford clearance); the ford clearance at forty marks and an autumn-road walk at sixty marks and fed both marked HOLD, Teague; a third hold's grain escort at thirty marked to an uncatalogued crew.

Pike's practice: a river stone as a one-handed paperweight worn pale into the plank; slips read silently, the witness mark checked against the hold's brand, then read aloud before entry and again after, with the in-world reason 'Half this meadow can't read. The book's for me. The saying's for them.'; short hirer remarks written in the margin ('I write the short ones'); a crew's rebuttal written and read aloud in the margin ('Crew says the bank went.'); Pike turning the ledger to face the unit ('It's your page'); HOLD plus the crew's name written beside a taken slip; 'No mark, no line.'

Two unnamed crews as background texture: a north-road escort crew (a woman captain with a bill-hook scar and three behind her) whose clean line is entered; a recovery crew whose captain stands at the plank while a partial failure is entered ('Eleven lost to the water. Nine recovered. Three marks of eight.') — the board's failure mode shown in scene.

Pike's carter's map on the plank: no seal, no dashes, the ford as dots, Lowmarch a square, roads as firm lines, holds marked by their brands with distances in days, and the Line drawn as a single unlabeled stroke at the left edge. No circles, blanks, or other Part 2 material.

Teague's three crew members as unnamed silhouettes (a tall woman with a spear, a broad man with a crossbow and a limp, a young man of about twenty) and the best table kept for them with a jug already on it; Teague's read of the room staged in Cael's method (Lira from her feet, Brom briefly, Karis at the wall, Seln found on the second pass, Cael last and longest). No facts about Teague beyond Path, lapsed Bronze tier, crew of four, three years at the top, and the counting habit the packet specifies; no age given.
Marks: eighteen earned across the four contracts, about ten left after the jug and loaf; the unit still sleeps in the meadow.
state_change_proposals: Timeline: Chapter 2 runs on the forty-ninth day past the Line, midday to dusk, at Lowmarch. The unit walked the Thornwater stretch back at midday without incident. Cael is eighteen; nine fragments plus the anomaly; deployment since the Line still none; Shadow-adjacent idle drift at dusk and Anchor-adjacent doorway pull noted again as idle texture only. No injuries.

Pike's ledger: the unit's page carries four completed lines; the fourth (Thornwater road) now bears a margin remark in Pike's hand, 'Hirer: knew to shut up.' The wall sheet at the lower inn lists thirteen crews; Teague's crew is first and the unit is thirteenth (eleven lines between), entered as five names rather than a crew name. Chapter 4's one-line move should start from this position.

Board state: sixteen postings; the ford clearance two days east (forty marks) and an autumn-road walk (sixty marks, fed) are marked HOLD, Teague; a third hold contract (grain escort, thirty marks) is held by an unnamed crew. Chapter 3's premise that the ford was priced for Teague's crew is consistent with this.

Knowledge state: the party now knows the board's full mechanism (posting by holds/brokers/carters, first-mark taking unless a hold names a crew, witness mark required, read aloud before and after entry, hirer-set price, Pike-ordered wall) and Teague's name, Path (Force), lapsed Bronze standing, crew of four, and three years at the top — from the board's HOLD marks and Pike's words. Cael and Teague have seen and read each other across the inn's room; neither has spoken to the other. Karis is copying the wall sheet and the map's brands into her notebook.

Third-party verdicts on record: Pike's spoken placement — 'Four lines. Nobody lost, nobody hurt, nobody knows you.' and 'Every job you've done was one nobody above you wanted.' Pike's pricing doctrine stated once, verbatim per the card.
The asset-restriction beat has been said once (Seln, Brom, Karis, over the carter's map) and the map turned east; per the packet it is not to be revisited in later chapters.
The arc's first pole is written in the log: 'No instrument out here reads me ... I'm free. First time.' — true at this altitude, to be complicated from Chapter 9.

Tic ledger for Book 7 after Chapter 2: 'There it was' registers one case-insensitive hit in this chapter, and it is the substring of the mandated Pike line ('In there it was heresy'); all other capped phrases zero; no standalone '[Name] noticed.'; no single-word paragraphs; 'the way ...' constructions all distinct.
deviations: Word count 5,169 against a 4,600 target — inside the 15% tolerance (ceiling 5,290) but above target, in line with Chapter 1's accepted 5,269. The overage is in the mechanism section (two slips entered in scene rather than one) and the itemized Teague read; either could be compressed if the editor wants the chapter closer to target.

The charter §9 grep for 'There it was' (case-insensitive) returns 1 for this chapter, but the hit is inside the packet's mandated verbatim line 'In there it was heresy.' There is no standalone 'There it was.' beat in the chapter. Reported so the book-level count is read correctly; the cap (3) is not threatened.

The packet's Karis line 'Nobody can. Different sentences.' and Seln's Line speech are rendered contiguously as written; Brom's 'Nobody wants to.' is preceded by an attribution clause ('Brom, from the roof's edge, without turning:') to satisfy the audio attribution rule in a three-speaker beat. No words of the mandated lines were altered.

Pike gives the tier fact in his own words ('Bronze — was, by the book inside. He stopped writing to it years ago and it stopped asking.') rather than the architecture's 'six years'; the packet's knowledge boundary says 'years ago' and the exact figure was left unstated to stay inside the invention budget.

The 'ledger on the wall' of the closing image is realized as a single sheet in Pike's hand — the ordered column of crews — pinned to the inn wall, distinct from the bound ledger on his table. This reading reconciles the packet's 'column' and 'ledger on the wall' with Chapter 1's ledger-as-book; if the editor prefers the bound ledger itself displayed, the change is confined to the room catalogue and the final paragraph.
